reference_sql:
SELECT p.brand, COUNT(*) AS n_products
FROM products p
JOIN (
  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) AS units
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY product_id
) AS u ON u.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE u.units > 2000
GROUP BY p.brand
alternatives:
WITH product_units AS (
  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) AS units
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.brand, COUNT(*) AS n_products
FROM products p
JOIN product_units u ON u.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE u.units > 2000
GROUP BY p.brand

SELECT p.brand, COUNT(*) AS n_products
FROM products p
JOIN (
  -- one row per product above 2,000 units
  SELECT product_id
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY product_id
  HAVING SUM(quantity) > 2000
) AS u ON u.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY p.brand

other_way.tradeoff: A WITH step holds the product totals under a name, which helps when a later step reads them again; here it only adds lines.
